def.short: the first meal of the day, eaten in the morning
def.long: The first meal of the day, usually eaten in the morning before work or school. It can be light (tea and toast) or large (eggs, cheese, olives, and more).

examples.en: I usually have breakfast at seven.
Ayşe made breakfast for the whole family.
examples.tr: Ayşe bütün aile için kahvaltı hazırladı.

examples.en: Breakfast is included in the hotel price.

etymology.text: From 'break' + 'fast': the meal that breaks the long overnight fast since dinner.

tr.note: Türkçedeki 'kahvaltı' da bir birleşik sözcüktür (kahve altı). İngilizcede öğün adlarından önce genellikle 'the' kullanılmaz.

mistakes.why: 'Kahvaltı yapmak' kalıbını 'do' ile kurmayın; İngilizcede 'have breakfast' denir ('make breakfast' = hazırlamak).

tr.mnemonic: Break + fast = orucu bozmak. İftar gibi, ama her sabah: gece boyu süren açlığı bozan öğün.

quiz.cloze: We usually eat ______ at 7 a.m., before school.

def.short: take something from someone and give it back later
def.long: To take something that belongs to someone else, with their permission, and return it after a time. You borrow FROM someone; the other person lends it TO you.

examples.en: Can I borrow your pen for a minute?
examples.tr: Kalemini bir dakikalığına ödünç alabilir miyim?

examples.en: She borrowed some money from her brother.
You can borrow up to five books from the library.
examples.tr: Kütüphaneden en fazla beş kitap ödünç alabilirsiniz.

etymology.text: From Old English 'borgian' (to borrow, lend, give a pledge), from 'borg', a pledge: borrowing once meant leaving something as a guarantee.

tr.note: Türkçede 'ödünç' hem alma hem verme için kullanılır (ödünç almak / ödünç vermek). İngilizcede iki ayrı fiil var: borrow = alan, lend = veren.

mistakes.wrong: Can you borrow me your pen?
mistakes.right: Can you lend me your pen? / Can I borrow your pen?
mistakes.why: 'Borrow' yalnızca alan kişi için; veren kişi 'lend' kullanır.

tr.mnemonic: Borrow ≈ BORÇ alırım. Borç alan 'borrow' der, borç veren 'lend'.

quiz.cloze: Could I ______ your charger? Mine is dead.

def.micro: bags and cases for a trip
def.short: the bags and suitcases you take with you when you travel
def.long: All the bags, suitcases, and boxes a traveler takes on a journey. 'Baggage' means almost the same and is common in airline English. It is uncountable: never 'luggages'.

examples.en: Please keep your luggage with you at all times.
examples.tr: Lütfen bagajınızı her zaman yanınızda tutun.

examples.en: The airline lost our luggage on the way to Izmir.
examples.tr: Havayolu şirketi, İzmir'e giderken bagajımızı kaybetti.

examples.en: Do you have any luggage to check in?

etymology.text: From 'lug' (to drag or carry with effort) + '-age': literally, the things you have to lug around.

tr.note: Türkçedeki 'bagaj' arabanın bagajı anlamına da gelir; İngilizcede araba bagajı 'trunk' (ABD) veya 'boot' (İngiltere)'dir, 'luggage' değildir.

mistakes.right: I have two bags. / two pieces of luggage
mistakes.why: 'Luggage' sayılamayan isimdir, çoğul eki almaz; sayı için 'bag' veya 'piece of luggage' kullanın.

tr.mnemonic: 'Lug' = sürükleyerek taşımak. Luggage = sürükleyip taşıdığın şeyler.

quiz.cloze: The airline lost my ______, so I had no clothes for the trip.

def.short: used to say what is really true, often when it is not what people expect
def.long: Used to show what is really true or what really happened, especially when it is surprising or different from what was expected. It does NOT mean 'at the moment' ('currently' or 'now' mean that).

examples.en: I thought the test would be hard, but it was actually quite easy.
examples.tr: Sınavın zor olacağını sanıyordum ama aslında oldukça kolaymış.

examples.en: Actually, I'd prefer tea, if that's okay.
examples.tr: Aslında çay tercih ederim, sakıncası yoksa.

examples.en: He looks shy, but he actually loves meeting new people.
examples.tr: Çekingen görünüyor ama aslında yeni insanlarla tanışmaya bayılıyor.

etymology.text: From 'actual', from Latin 'actus' (a doing, a deed): 'actually' = in deed, in real fact, not just in theory.

tr.note: Türkçedeki 'aktüel' = 'güncel'. İngilizce 'actual/actually' ise 'gerçek/aslında' demektir. 'Şu anda' için 'currently' veya 'at the moment' kullanılır.

mistakes.wrong: The actual price of petrol is very high.
mistakes.right: The current price of petrol is very high.

mistakes.wrong: Actually I'm studying English. (= şu anda)
mistakes.why: 'Actually' zaman bildirmez; 'şu anda' için 'currently / at the moment'.

tr.mnemonic: ACT = eylem: 'actually' = fiilen, gerçekte. 'Aktüel' (güncel) tuzağına düşme.

quiz.cloze: He looks young, but he is ______ forty.

def.micro: last time to finish a task
def.short: the latest date or time by which something must be finished
def.long: A fixed date or time by which a task must be completed or handed in. Missing a deadline can have consequences, such as a penalty or a lost opportunity.

examples.en: The deadline for the report is Friday at noon.
examples.tr: Raporun son teslim tarihi cuma günü öğlen.

examples.en: We worked all night to meet the deadline.
examples.tr: Son teslim tarihine yetişmek için bütün gece çalıştık.

examples.en: She asked for a deadline extension.

etymology.text: First a line around a US Civil War prison camp that prisoners could not cross. The 'time limit' sense came later (printing); the link between the two is only indirectly documented.

tr.note: Gündelik iş dilinde Türkçede de 'deadline' aynen kullanılır; resmî yazıda 'son teslim tarihi' tercih edin.

mistakes.right: The deadline is Friday. / We must finish by Friday.
mistakes.why: Türkçedeki 'cumaya kadar' kalıbı 'until' ile çevrilir; ama bitiş anı için 'by' kullanılır.

quiz.cloze: The project is late, so we asked for a new ______.
